recentItems.title: Iraq devalues currency by 15% as Hormuz crisis disrupts oil exports
recentItems.description:
Iraq has devalued its currency by around 15%, the biggest adjustment since 2020. 
The change is the Iraqi government’s response to disrupted oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz the country’s dependence on food imports means essential items like rice and flour are expected to become more expensive. 

Al Jazeera’s Peter Smith reports from Baghdad, Iraq.

recentItems.title: Houthi airport attacks will not weaken Saudi Arabia, analyst says
recentItems.description:
Yemen's Houthi movement says it now considers Saudi airspace a "theatre of military operations".
They are also warning international airlines to stop flying to the kingdom.
Earlier, Saudia Arabia confirmed the deaths of three foreign nationals in attacks at two separate international airports.

Khaled Batarfi, Saudi political analyst and author, tells Al Jazeera that the Houthis have made similar threats to Saudi Arabia before but argues the country is better equipped to defend itself now.

recentItems.title: Through Misan Harriman’s Lens: Stories of Resistance from around the world | Witness Documentary
recentItems.description:
British Nigerian visual storyteller Misan Harriman is renowned for his wide-ranging work, including powerful breakthrough images from the 2020 Black Lives Matter protests and the Palestinian protest movement.

He made history as the first Black man to shoot a British Vogue cover and has photographed a range of celebrities, including Angelina Jolie, Lewis Hamilton, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle. Through an exploration of the resilience of grassroots activists fighting for equality, civil rights and social justice around the world, Harriman's lens brings the world's activism to light, revealing the power of collective action in shaping a more just society.

Shoot the People is a documentary film by Andy Mundy-Castle.

recentItems.title: Russian glide bomb hits buses in Ukraine's Kramatorsk, killing at least 30
recentItems.description:
A Russian strike has killed at least 30 people in Ukraine's eastern city of Kramatorsk, according to the regional governor.
Police say two passenger buses were struck by a Russian glide bomb.
Russian forces have stepped up attacks on Kramatorsk as they try to push further into Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. 

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

recentItems.title: Israeli army, settlers target Palestinian olive harvest in occupied West Bank
recentItems.description:
Once a joyous season, the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank has become a time of fear and danger. 
Armed Israeli settlers are attacking Palestinians and Israeli forces are banning families from accessing their own lands. 

Al Jazeera’s Nida Ibrahim reports from Ramallah in the occupied West Bank.

recentItems.title: Signs and plaques removed from UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem
recentItems.description:
Signs and plaques have been removed at the British consulate in occupied East Jerusalem
Israel's foreign minister ordered the consulate to close in response to British sanctions on goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The consulate oversees the UK's relationship with Palestinians. The closure order does not impact the British embassy in Tel Aviv.
But Britain says the consulate will remain open as a UK Mission.

Al Jazeera’s Camille Nedelec reports from London, UK

recentItems.title: Eritrea denies troop deployment in Ethiopia as fighting escalates
recentItems.description:
Eritrean soldiers have reportedly been seen driving through northern Ethiopia.
Eritrea denies that its troops have crossed the border town of Zelambessa.
The alleged sightings come as fighting intensifies between government forces and the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).
Ethiopia has accused Egypt, Eritrea and Sudan of supporting an armed alliance of opposition groups.
All three countries deny involvement.

Al Jazeera’s Malcolm Webb reports from Nairobi, Kenya.

Alan Boswell is the Horn of Africa Director at the International Crisis Group. He says that a reported incursion of Eritrean forces into Ethiopia could push the two countries into war.
